items.summary: The Land Transport Authority responded to Andre Ching Wei Jie’s Oct 29 letter calling for effective enforcement of new bus regulations. Senior Group Director Yeo Teck Guan explained that captains prioritise safe driving over enforcing against nuisance behaviour, but can seek support from the bus operations control centre, which may activate police or require disruptive passengers to alight. Captains and authorised staff are empowered to take action, and commuters can report incidents via an online feedback form; verified cases allow follow-up even after a passenger leaves.
items.title: LTA Outlines Measures Against Nuisance Behaviour on Buses

items.summary: Chong Ryh Huei wrote that protecting personal data must take priority over efficiency and AI adoption. She cited a recent article about a 9½-hour public healthcare service outage on Oct 13 caused by a missed security update, alongside the Alliance Medinet data breach and National Cancer Centre Singapore e-mail lapse as concerns for safeguarding citizens' information. She called for effective implementation of ISO standards, AI verification tools and Health Ministry guidelines, with independent testing before expanding AI access to sensitive systems.
items.title: Personal data protection should take priority over AI adoption, says Chong Ryh Huei

items.summary: The International Federation of the Phonographic Industry (IFPI), the global peak body for the music recording industry, warned that Australia weakening copyright protections for AI companies would be “ridiculous and dangerous”. IFPI CEO Victoria Oakley told Guardian Australia that accepting such demands could throw away Australian culture and creativity. Labor is considering a suite of policy changes around AI, including datacentres, online safety, workforce, energy and the economy. The attorney general, Michelle Rowland, said via a spokesperson last week that the government was “committed to supporting” creatives. Oakley declined to speculate on legal or constitutional challenges but warned it could damage Australia’s standing in the creative world.
items.title: IFPI warns weakening AI copyright law risks creativity

items.summary: Steven Strogatz and Alex Townsend, mathematics professors at Cornell University, argue that the relentless pursuit of optimisation can backfire by weakening a system's robustness. They illustrate this with England's hospital beds: about 95% were occupied during last year's flu season, leaving little reserve for surges. A second trap is an overly narrow definition of 'best', exemplified by Milton Keynes' roundabouts that prioritise traffic flow over passenger comfort. The third arises when optimising parts produces collective failure, as seen in the May 2010 US market crash triggered partly by automated trading worth more than $4bn. They warn AI could make all three traps worse and urges deciding what 'best' truly means rather than optimising away essential slack.
items.title: Mathematicians Warn That Over-Optimisation Undermines System Robustness

items.summary: Japanese manufacturer Iris Ohyama disclosed that personal information belonging to about 7. 7 million people may have been exposed after unauthorized access to a third-party cloud service used by its Iris Plaza shopping platform. The company discovered the incident late last month and publicly notified Japan's Personal Information Protection Commission and police on October 29, 2026. It said up to 5. 8 million registered members and former members plus 1. 9 million non-members may be affected, while still determining exact record counts. Exposed data could include names, addresses, phone numbers, email addresses, gender, birth dates and passwords; credit card information was not stored there.
items.title: Iris Ohyama Discloses Data Cloud Breach Affecting Millions of Customers

items.summary: A record-low water level at Lake Powell, on the Utah-Arizona border, has intensified calls to drain the reservoir through new diversion tunnels below Glen Canyon Dam. Advocates such as the Glen Canyon Institute promote a plan called Fill Mead First, which would boost hydropower in Lake Mead and restore Glen Canyon's formations and wildlife while reducing evaporative losses of roughly 11 percent annually. Officials inspected the bypass tubes in 2025 and said they might work if needed, though critics warn of structural damage risk and note that a full study could take about a decade at billions of dollars. The federal government did not consider draining Powell in its environmental impact statement finalized in August for managing the river over the next 10 years.
items.title: Colorado River Drought Drives Debate Over Draining Lake Powell

items.summary: The New York Public Service Commission approved two utility thermal energy network plans expected to cost $111.5 million, while rejecting nine others including several in New York City. The Haverstraw project would receive $50 million investment and connect up to 30 structures; the Buffalo project uses an existing steam heat system. National Fuel Gas will shift from natural gas by combining borehole water with wastewater heat recovery for low-income housing. A separate Metropolitan Transportation Authority feasibility study costs $800,000 to assess subway platform cooling in Lower Manhattan. The UpgradeNY coalition advocates replacing gas pipelines with thermal networks using heat pumps and waste heat sources.
items.title: New York Approves Utility Thermal Energy Networks for Clean Heating

items.summary: The article centers on reports that Volkswagen is considering rolling out its China-developed electrical architecture across most of its European markets, a move tied to the recently revealed ID. AURA L5 electric sedan and VW Group's broader software push at this year's China International Import Expo (CIIE). Citing Autocar and Reuters, the piece quotes Thomas Schäfer, Volkswagen brand CEO: “up to 75% of the firm’s core models in Europe could eventually use the China Electronic Architecture.” The item frames the ID. AURA L5 as a potential mainstream rival to Tesla's Model 3 and notes VW is also seeking outside software help from Rivian for its Scout truck, underscoring ongoing struggles with vehicle software delivery.
items.title: Volkswagen Weighs Chinese Software for European Models

items.summary: CleanTechnica reports that California’s ports of Los Angeles and Long Beach, in their Clean Marine Fuel Feasibility Assessment released in October, left hydrogen out of detailed deep-sea shipping plans. Of 38 shipping lines contacted, 19 responded; nine showed interest or commitment for methanol but only one for hydrogen. The authors note the survey reflects carrier intentions rather than binding contracts and that a single interested carrier does not justify expensive hydrogen infrastructure. Long Beach offers a $1 million incentive for an initial commercial-scale methanol bunkering operation instead. The piece frames this as California applying a commercial filter to fuel planning.
items.title: California Ports Skip Hydrogen for Deep-Sea Shipping

items.summary: A Mercer study projects total health benefit cost per employee rising 8.2% in 2027, the highest increase since 2003, even after planned employer cost reductions that would otherwise lift existing plans about 11%. The Wall Street Journal reported employees' share of these costs has risen faster still. Mercer's author argues employers have alternatives like individual coverage health reimbursement arrangements and health savings accounts, noting ICHRA adoption grew between 73% and 128% among firms with fewer than 100 employees, yet most simply pass rising costs to workers.
items.title: Employers Pass Rising Healthcare Costs to Workers Despite Available Alternatives

items.summary: Fresh HMRC information obtained through a freedom of information request shows the UK spent at least £100m on Brexit border inspection posts that were never used. Seven inland facilities in England and Wales were built but quickly decommissioned after the government decided not to implement all planned checks, concluding EU food standards would remain unchanged. Dover white cliffs alone cost the taxpayer £28m while remaining a field; total operational costs have run to £179m. HMRC noted Birmingham, Ebbsfleet and North Weald did not require land acquisition. Portsmouth's £23m post now faces an uncertain future as ports call for compensation when checks end.
items.title: UK Border Inspection Posts Cost Taxpayers £179m

items.summary: A new Climate Trends report says food waste costs India about $1.3 billion yearly, driven by weak cold storage and poor weather; roughly 40% of fruit and vegetables spoil before reaching buyers. It recommends expanding cold-chain access and better weather warnings.
items.title: Climate Trends Report Flags India's Food-Waste Loss

items.summary: Shamika Ravi, a member of the Prime Minister's Economic Advisory Council (EAC-PM), told Business Today Group Editor Siddharth Zarabi that India's attraction to public employment traces partly to its feudal past. She said the preference was strongest in states where economic growth and private-sector transitions had been slower.
items.title: Economist Ravi on India's enduring preference for government jobs

items.summary: After a visit to Uruguay, Pope Leo XIV is heading to Argentina for the second leg of his tour. In Florida he celebrated the feast of the Virgin of the Thirty-three and thanked mothers who passed on the faith. The trip comes amid sharp criticism from the Argentine Catholic Church over President Javier Milei's austerity program, which has slashed healthcare spending by 48% in real terms since December 2023. Official data put poverty at 32.3% of Argentines during the first half of 2026, about 15 million people. Leo is seen as continuing the work left unfinished by Pope Francis, who never returned home from Argentina.
items.title: Pope Leo XIV Begins South American Tour in Uruguay

items.summary: Abdulla Balalaa, UAE Assistant Minister of Foreign Affairs for Energy and Sustainability, argues that water cooperation can redefine diplomacy by uniting countries around shared challenges. Writing on the run-up to the 2026 UN Water Conference in Abu Dhabi, he notes no single institution holds all expertise or capital needed for resilience. He cites the Taweelah Independent Water Plant—built by PowerChina and producing around 900,000 cubic meters of freshwater per day—as evidence of UAE-China collaboration, plus a May 2025 memorandum signed between the Mohamed bin Zayed Water Initiative and China's Institute of Seawater Desalination. Balalaa contends cooperation should be judged by results rather than agreements alone, calling on governments, businesses and civil society to translate ambition into lasting impact before December.
items.title: UAE Foreign Minister Frames Water Cooperation as Diplomatic Opportunity

items.summary: At St Columb’s Hall in Derry on Saturday night, the Foyle Rumble brought together dozens of performers for a wrestling show blending athleticism with scripted storytelling. Many participants have learning or physical disabilities and create stage personae that they say carry them into real life; Keelan O’Hagan described how his ring character Kellio never quits after being bullied, while blind Brian Walsh said the training was scary at first but to be a blind wrestler is “the best thing ever.” The Foyle Rumble is run by the Tuned In Project and Complete Anarchy Wrestling (CAW), which aim to give disabled people more independence. Organisers say participants have grown in confidence since the inaugural 2024 show, though Conn warned that despite being choreographed there has been real risk with students bruised and battered.
items.title: Disabled Wrestlers Find Confidence Through Ring Alter Egos in Derry Show

items.summary: Brighton & Hove Albion beat ten-man Brentford 2-0 at the Amex, with Diego Gomez scoring in the 15th minute and Pascal Gross converting a penalty in the 42nd. The red card to Thiago came after a VAR check following a tussle with Chema Andres. Brighton head into the international break on 22 points, behind Arsenal's 27, moving above Manchester City into second place.
items.title: Brighton Move Second With Victory Over Ten-Man Brentford

items.summary: Comedian Russell Brand is set to receive a prison sentence after being found guilty on three counts of sexual assault and one of rape following a four-week trial. Judge Joel Bennathan warned him he faced a significant custodial term, denying bail so he could spend the weekend with his children in London jail. Danny Shaw estimated 4-13 years.
items.title: Russell Brand Faces Prison Sentence After Rape Conviction

items.summary: Carlos Alcaraz won the Paris Masters on Sunday by edging Ben Shelton 7-6(5) 7-5 to claim his ninth ATP 1000 title. The world number three avenged a US Open last-eight loss and became the first Spaniard to win since David Ferrer in 2012, controlling play from the baseline while Shelton struggled with an erratic forehand.
items.title: Alcaraz wins Paris Masters, ninth ATP 1000 title

items.summary: A beef industry-funded science curriculum quietly removed a lesson on cattle methane and climate after ranchers disputed its premise, the Guardian reports. The American Farm Bureau Foundation for Agriculture produces free materials used by around 1.2m students across more than 100 school districts nationwide. A spokesperson said the topic “cannot be a 45-minute lesson” but is working on a longer version with unnamed researchers. Rancher Jim Mundorf sparked the backlash, calling blaming cattle for climate change comparable to blaming volcanoes or lightning strikes. Climate scientists note biogenic methane maintains about 0.3C of global warming and that livestock accounts for roughly 2% versus the true figure over 30%. The National Center for Science Education warned the episode suggests producer needs prevail in curriculum decisions, while a University of Miami study found decades-old industry efforts to downplay cattle emissions.
items.title: Beef Industry Scraps Methane Lesson After Rancher Backlash

items.summary: FRANCE 24 looks back at some of the week's most striking images, covering Democratic Party wins in the US midterm elections, France's ongoing student-led protests, and the first Olympic sports event held on African soil.
items.title: FRANCE 24 Reviews Week's Striking Images Across Three Stories

items.summary: Following the Fifth Plenary Session of the 20th CPC Central Committee, officials are expected to advance full and rigorous Communist Party self-governance. The goal is for policies to reach ordinary citizens through more affordable medicines, safer food, faster government services, and reduced red tape, delays, and corruption.
items.title: CPC Calls for Stricter Party Self-Governance After Plenary Session

items.summary: A Brazilian biologist and volunteer divers are manually removing sun coral, an invasive species first seen in Brazil more than 40 years ago, from an offshore oil platform near Ipanema beach. The team says the coral has no natural predators there, has spread along the coast, and could suffocate marine wildlife. Adriana Gomes described their method as simple but effective: using their own hands. A video shows whether they succeed.
items.title: Brazilian Divers Remove Invasive Coral by Hand

items.summary: A rare double waterspout formed over the Italian island of Capri on Saturday, with two swirling columns emerging from heavy clouds above its Faraglioni rock formations. The event created a striking natural spectacle. Waterspouts are relatively common over the Mediterranean in late summer and autumn when cooler air moves over warmer waters.
items.title: Rare Double Waterspout Forms Over Italy's Capri Island

items.summary: The drivers' championship is sealed, but the final four rounds remain contested as teams chase prize money. Oscar Piastri starts 10th while Lando Norris takes pole alongside world champion Kimi Antonelli, who spun off before the race amid wet conditions in São Paulo.
items.title: F1 Set for Wet São Paulo Race After World Champion Spins Off

items.summary: Two trains collided south of Cairo, killing at least four people and injuring another 88 on Sunday, according to the authorities. The accident occurred in Al Ayyat, Giza province, about 52 kilometres south of Cairo, when a train heading toward Fayum struck the rear of one bound for Aswan; one derailed but its identity was not specified. Egyptian President Abdelfatah al-Sisi ordered an investigation into causes and responsibility.
items.title: Egyptian President Orders Probe After Two Trains Collide Near Cairo

items.summary: On Sunday, Poland launched a terror probe into the mass shooting in Krakow that occurred the day before. The attack left six people killed and many more injured. Authorities said the 24-year-old suspect used a semi-automatic rifle and was fascinated by far-right ideologies. He remains in critical condition in hospital.
items.title: Poland Launches Terror Probe After Six Killed in Krakow Far-Right Shooting

items.summary: Two trains collided south of the Egyptian capital on Sunday, derailing several carriages. The health ministry counted four passengers killed with 88 others being treated near Giza, while State-owned media earlier reported 120 wounded without clarifying severity. President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi said he was following it 'with great concern' and directed an urgent investigation to hold accountable anyone found negligent.
items.title: Egypt: 4 dead and dozens injured after two trains collide south of Cairo

items.summary: Police in Ceuta are introducing a new identification procedure as authorities dismantle temporary migrant camps, relocating residents to other facilities afterward. The enclave has seven camps, with plans to move migrants between them and close smaller ones. A large July influx from Morocco reignited the immigration debate across Spain and Europe.
items.title: Ceuta Police Launch New ID Process for Migrants at Camps

items.summary: European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen said EU flags were flying at half-mast in tribute to the victims and first responders after a Saturday shooting near Krakow's Main Market Square left six people dead and 16 injured. She stressed European unity, calling the solidarity 'Stronger than hatred.' Polish Interior Minister Marcin Kierwinski noted preliminary findings suggested far-right influence, though unverified.
items.title: EU Flags at Half-Mast After Deadly Krakow Shooting

items.summary: Lionel Messi became the first player in Major League Soccer history to win back-to-back Golden Boots, claiming the 2026 scoring title with 26 goals and 17 assists for a league-leading 43 goal contributions. The 39-year-old finished ahead of Petar Musa (22) and Sam Surridge (21). Messi previously won in 2025 with 29 goals, joining six prior two-time winners.
items.title: Messi Wins Second Straight MLS Golden Boot

items.summary: EL PAÍS reports that dozens of Ethiopian nationals are awaiting execution by beheading in the Khamis Mushait prison in Saudi Arabia, many from Tigray. The piece centers on Dawit Tesfay, a 24-year-old who has spent eight months awaiting execution after an account-described trial lasting two minutes with no lawyer or interpreter; his final phone words to EL PAÍS express uncertainty about surviving the next day. Human Rights Watch documents that at least 20 Ethiopians were executed for drug trafficking between January and August 2026, with another 76 facing imminent risk. Amnesty International records 96 executions in Saudi Arabia through June 22, 2026, of which 61 were drug-related and 39 foreign nationals. A researcher notes at least 36 Ethiopians executed in 2025, with 20 this year for smuggling hashish, while Human Rights Watch says 2025 saw 356 executions overall, the highest on record. Families, regional authorities and organizations demand legal counsel, fair trials and repatriation; the Ethiopian Ministry of Foreign Affairs cites 1,971 citizens who benefited from royal pardons but received no response to EL PAÍS's request for its position.
items.title: Ethiopians on Saudi Death Row Appeal for Rescue and Fair Trials

items.summary: In Tuesday's midterms, Democratic candidates won all 10 congressional districts along the U.S.-Mexico border, reversing a trend where Donald Trump held strong support there in 2024. Two Texas districts flipped parties. Every counted district swung toward Democrats with a median shift of 23 percentage points versus 14.1 nationwide. James Talarico leads by 55.8 points in Starr County, once a Republican stronghold since 1892.
items.title: Democrats Win All U.S.-Mexico Border Congressional Districts in Midterms

items.summary: Bangkok will host Eurovision's inaugural Asia contest on November 14, featuring K-pop and Bangladeshi beatboxing. Eleven countries compete across Laos, Mongolia and the Philippines. The event airs live on television and YouTube, though uncertainty remains over whether audiences will tune in.
items.title: Eurovision launches first Asia edition in Bangkok with regional acts

items.summary: SoftBank Group and ABB are exploring carving out the Chinese part of a robotics deal blocked by Beijing, according to people familiar with the matter. The Office of the Working Mechanism for Foreign Investment Sec 5 halted SoftBank's move Thursday to acquire the $5.4 billion ABB unit on Thursday. The companies and advisers are studying how China’s business could be separated as SoftBank leads private talks.
items.title: SoftBank and ABB Explore China Carve-Out for Robotics Deal

items.summary:
The Dominican Republic opposes deep-sea mining, arguing that marine ecosystems are the country’s greatest natural and strategic riches. Jonathan Delance of the National 30×30 Program calls them “greatest natural and strategic riches,” while Edward Pérez Reyes presented a moratorium position at ISA Assembly in July 2023, urging science to advance before commercial exploitation. Environmental groups, including the Magua Ecological Foundation’s Manuel Alejandro Rodríguez, warn impacts could be severe and irreversible. The country protected 30.8 percent of its waters in 2024. Delance stresses that precautionary protection is needed first.

visual null
items.title: Dominican Republic Backs Pause on Deep-Sea Mining

items.summary: In New Delhi, Prime Minister Narendra Modi visited former deputy prime minister Lal Krishna Advani at his residence to greet him on his birthday. The veteran BJP leader entered his 100th year. Party members held a havan ceremony and attended the event between 10am and 10.30am.
items.title: Modi Visits Advani on His Birthday as He Enters 100th Year

items.summary: Congress leader Sonia Gandhi described her memoir Belonging: A Journey of Love as personal rather than political ahead of its India release on November 10. In an article for The Hindu, she said much had been written about her family but rarely with real insight into who they were and their struggles. She wanted to portray them honestly as people she knew and loved.
items.title: Sonia Gandhi Frames Her Memoir as Personal, Not Political

items.summary: A senior Democrat said Elon Musk and White House chief of staff Stephen Miller are likely targets of congressional investigations after Democrats win control in January. Robert Garcia cited Musk's role in the Department of Government Efficiency firings and Miller as architect of an unpopular immigration crackdown, which a Reuters/Ipsos poll showed fell to 37 per cent from 50 per cent at Trump's start.
items.title: Democrats Signal Probes of Musk, Miller After Midterm Gains

items.summary: The Russian Defence Ministry said overnight strikes hit three cargo vessels carrying military goods for Ukraine, including ships bound for the ports of Odesa and Chornomorsk, plus two power substations in Dnipropetrovsk and Zhytomyr regions. Reuters could not independently verify these claims, and there was no immediate comment from Ukraine. Ukrainian company DTEK said an overnight attack left more than 600,000 people without electricity.
items.title: Russia Claims Strikes on Ukraine Ships and Power Grid

items.summary: More than eight months into the war between the United States and Iran, several countries have stepped forward to broker a deal (s0). Qatar is now positioning itself as a key mediator after previously distancing itself from direct mediation following Iranian attacks. Qatari Prime Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman bin Jassim Al Thani said during an Oxford University interview that mediation efforts remain active and warned the crisis “cannot be left unresolved” (s5, s6). The remarks came a day after Reuters reported Iran had sent the US a nuclear proposal via Qatar. Doha's re-engagement follows earlier reluctance; in March its foreign ministry told Reuters there was no direct Qatari mediation, but it later hosted Iranian delegations and visited Washington twice to discuss de-escalation (s12, s13, s23).
items.title: Qatar Emerges as Key Mediator in US-Iran Talks

items.summary: In a U-19 Asia Cup match, Pakistan chased down India's total of 208 to win by three wickets. Hamza Zahoor scored an unbeaten 100 off 108 balls after coming in at number seven and guided the chase home. Arjun Rajput top-scored for India with 107 off 85 balls, while Manal Chauhan took 3/32 for her side.
items.title: Pakistan Edge India in U-19 Asia Cup Chase

items.summary: Kevin John Brophy, Emeritus Professor of Creative Writing at The University of Melbourne, reviews Christian Ryan’s new book Eleven: We Burn Them in the Sun. He describes Ryan as a gifted writer with a passion for cricket and its expansive room for life beyond sport. His earlier biography of Kim Hughes was voted the best cricketing book ever by Wisden Cricket Monthly. In his new work, Ryan weaves together at least 11 men and women whose lives were defined briefly by cricket, moving between them without chapter breaks or a clear through-line. Brophy warns it may be unreadable, yet hopes Ryan will one day be adopted as a national treasure. The article first appeared on The Conversation.
items.title: A reviewer calls Christian Ryan’s cricket book a national treasure

items.summary: An Ohio appeals court upheld a ruling letting Stephen Ellison keep sole ownership of an Elbrook Avenue house he bought in 2012, before his September 2018 marriage. The panel rejected the wife's claim that mortgage payments made with shared funds turned it into marital property, noting rental income covered those payments and kept ownership traceable under Ohio law. It also upheld a $20,000 legal fee order against her after she dragged out proceedings; the husband's lawyer had spent more than $56,000 on fees over two years. The unanimous decision ends their appeals process.
items.title: Ohio Court Upholds Pre-Marital Home Ownership and Fee Award

items.summary: On Thursday, California Governor Gavin Newsom commuted the death sentences of all 548 people awaiting execution in the state. The move is widely seen as his last major action before a possible resignation to run for president in 2028, though he cannot run in 2026 due to term limits. On Polymarket, Newsom holds an 11% chance of winning the Democratic nomination, behind Jon Ossoff (26%) and AOC (17%).
items.title: California Governor Gavin Newsom Commutes Death Sentences Amid 2028 Presidential Ambitions

items.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi celebrated Diwali with security forces in Bastar, Chhattisgarh, describing it as a historic victory over decades of Naxalism and Maoist terror. He praised the sacrifices of security personnel and said every district is now free from Naxal influence. Modi also cited 50 crore Indians lifted from extreme poverty across 12 years through welfare schemes, while warning against complacency amid continuing ideological infiltration by Naxals.
items.title: Modi Marks Naxalism Victory at Bastar Diwali With Security Forces

items.summary: Superstar Rajinikanth marked Diwali by greeting fans outside his residence in traditional clothing, offering festive wishes. Noticing impending rain, he pointed to the sky and advised admirers to return home safely. The item also reports unrelated political tensions between Yogi Adityanath and Akhilesh Yadav over an Ayodhya visit.
items.title: Rajinikanth Greets Fans and Warns of Rain During Diwali

items.summary: An Ohio appeals court upheld a $45,806 payment owed by a homeowner to a contractor after the owner refused final payment over visible defects in newly built basement walls. The judges found the concrete foundation structurally sound and meeting building codes despite cosmetic flaws like honeycombing and an uneven finish. Under Ohio law's substantial performance rule, minor surface problems do not justify withholding full payment when the structure is safe and functional.
items.title: Ohio Court Orders Homeowner to Pay Contractor for Basement Work

items.summary: Live air quality data from AQI. in showed that on Diwali evening, six Indian cities recorded an AQI above 1,000. Sri Ganganagar in Rajasthan led with a hazardous reading of 1131, followed by Chengalpattu and Chennai (1122 and 1119), Bhubaneswar in Odisha (1091), Faridkot in Punjab (1058) and Puducherry (1057). The top 150 most polluted cities worldwide were dominated by Indian urban centres, with only Lahore and a few Nepali cities as exceptions. Chennai held the No. 1 position for much of the late evening. Contrary to expectation, Delhi did not appear in the top 25 at 8.
items.title: Diwali pollution leaves Indian cities at top of world’s most-polluted list

items.summary: Actress Rashmika Mandanna shared festive messages on Instagram, extending her Diwali wishes to fans along with photos of family time. In a video message she wished followers a happy Diwali and hoped they would find happiness in both little and big things, adding good health, joy and endless love. She also posted pictures posing with actor Vijay Deverakonda and with Anand Deverakonda.
items.title: Rashmika Mandanna Shares Diwali Wishes For Fans

items.summary: Police said a 33-year-old Sashastra Seema Bal (SSB) jawan was allegedly found dead while on duty at the Khanuwa Border Outpost under SSB's 66th Battalion during the intervening night of Saturday and Sunday, around 1.40am, in Uttar Pradesh's Maharajganj district. The sound of a gunshot alerted fellow personnel who rushed to find him critically injured; he later died. Nautanwa circle officer Basant Singh said police received information about the death and dispatched a team immediately. Preliminary information suggests emotional distress following his elder brother's death around two-and-a-half months ago, but exact circumstances remain under investigation.
items.title: SSB jawan found dead at India-Nepal border outpost in UP

items.summary: Police recovered the remains of two additional victims in the Bengaluru serial murder case from a forest area near Chamundi Hill in Mysuru on Sunday, raising the total number of bodies found so far to five. The accused Indushekhar had supplied information leading to the discovery; the bodies were stuffed into gunny bags and tied. Police continue searching for two remaining victims.
items.title: Bengaluru serial murder suspect linked to two more bodies near Chamundi Hill

items.summary: The US has launched a 20-member task force, Task Force Iron Gate, to disrupt weapons shipments and illicit trade through Iran's land borders and the Caspian Sea. CENTCOM chief Admiral Brad Cooper said it reinforces the naval blockade against Iran at sea. The move follows Iranian threats of retaliation beyond the Middle East.
items.title: US Deploys Task Force Iron Gate Against Iran's Land Routes

items.summary: An opinion piece denounces the Panchayati Raj minister's proposal to accept only voter cards for panchayat benefits, calling it an attempt to exclude people from schemes such as MGNREGA and PM-KISAN. The author frames it as a back-door National Registry of Citizens move that could create statelessness, noting about 13 crore people have been deleted from electoral rolls.
items.title: Commentator condemns voter-ID welfare rule as Hindu Rashtra plot

items.summary: Villagers near Karjat in Raigad district oppose Torrent Power’s proposed 3,000 MW pumped-storage hydroelectric project at Saidongar, fearing deforestation and water loss. The site requires 377 hectares including over 233 of forest and 144 of private land. Forest Officer Sameer Shinde said 2,700 trees were cut before work stopped after protests. Residents dispute the environmental assessment and demand cancellation.
items.title: Villagers Protest Torrent Power’s Saidongar Hydro Project Over Tree Felling

items.summary: Delhi's air quality was rated 'very poor' on Sunday, with the average AQI at 376 across 59 monitoring stations that recorded data. Twelve stations fell into the 'severe' category and 22 into 'very poor'. The worst reading came in Jahangirpuri at 463. Air quality is forecast to worsen to 'severe' on Monday after Diwali celebrations, vehicular emissions, and peak stubble-burning season. Unfavourable weather conditions are also aggravating the situation.
items.title: Delhi Air Quality Deteriorates Ahead of Diwali

items.summary: A report by EY says companies must integrate artificial intelligence into existing business systems rather than relying on isolated applications to improve customer service. The firm outlines five steps, from scaling high-impact processes to measuring real business outcomes like cost and revenue instead of tracking adoption or task counts. It stresses continuous investment in data, governance and workforce readiness for lasting value. EY notes the path differs across organizations but successful ones share a common approach: operating services atop integrated systems rather than standalone pilots, which it says leads to better results.
items.title: EY Warns AI Deployment Alone Won't Improve Customer Service

items.summary: On Sunday morning, Delhi recorded an overall Air Quality Index of 383 at 8 am per the Sameer application. Twenty-four monitoring stations exceeded AQI 400, with Jahangirpuri worst at 450, followed by RK Puram at 448 and Punjabi Bagh at 446. Neighbouring Noida reached 319 and Gurugram 322. Firecrackers, stubble burning in Punjab and Haryana, vehicular pollution and falling temperatures are cited as causes.
items.title: Delhi Air Hits Severe Pollution on Diwali Morning

items.summary: On Diwali morning, Delhi recorded an AQI of 384, placing it in the very poor category near severe. Several National Capital Region areas reported unhealthy air while Mumbai stayed moderate at 129. Monitoring stations above 400 included Jahangirpuri at a PM2.5 level of 450 and India Gate at 398. Delhi's air was forecast to remain severe on 8 and 9 November, with experts citing firecrackers, vehicle pollution, stubble burning and low wind speeds as causes.
items.title: Delhi Air Quality Stays Very Poor on Diwali Eve

items.summary: The Nationalist Congress Party remains split between two factions after Ajit Pawar's January 2026 death, with no formal merger completed. Senior leaders offer contradictory accounts: Sunil Tatkare says reunification would have been set for 12 February but his death halted it, while Anil Deshmukh rules out a merger entirely. BJP interest and meetings with Union Home Minister Amit Shah and Prime Minister Narendra Modi fuel speculation, though clarity awaits a proposed meeting between Sharad Pawar and Praful Patel.
items.title: NCP Merger Talks Stall on Conflicting Statements

items.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi extended Diwali greetings across India from a post on X on Sunday, November 8, wishing people happiness and prosperity. He said he would continue his tradition of celebrating the festival among jawans at the border. Earlier that day, he met Vice President CP Radhakrishnan to exchange wishes as five-day celebrations began with Dhanteras.
items.title: Modi Greets Nation on Diwali, Spends Festival with Border Soldiers
